items.title: Amazon's God Of War Has Cast The Perfect Actress As Faye
items.content:
Deborah Ann Woll's Faye is too crucial to simply recast.

There are some video games that are just so successful that the inevitability of an adaptation is inescapable. Although it took Halo 21 years and eight games to finally get a streaming series in 2022, a live-action adaptation of the games had been in the works in some fashion since 2005. It only took Resident Evil five years to receive a big budget theatrical release that spurred on a long-running franchise. Meanwhile, Tomb Raider, Mortal Kombat , Uncharted, and Assassin’s Creed got film adaptations, while even projects based on Call of Duty and Battlefield are on the way.

However, one of the franchises that has been at the top of that list for a very long time is the God of War series. Since the original game released back in 2005, there have been discussions about a live-action attempt (Universal Studios was interested the exact same year the game came out), but now that the series is in the current Norse-era of releases, it seems like those aspirations are finally about to come to fruition. Amazon Studios is currently deep in production on an adaptation of the recent God of War games , and a bit of casting news has just revealed that a familiar face from the games is about to carry over into the show.

After failing multiple times to bring the original Greek trilogy to the big screen, Hollywood has found the perfect angle with a streaming adaptation of the Norse-era games instead.

Earlier today, Variety revealed that actress Deborah Ann Woll would be reprising her role as Faye in Amazon’s upcoming TV adaptation of 2018’s God of War and its sequel God of War: Ragnarok. It’s yet another piece of major casting news, coming only a few months after the reveal that Dave Bautista would be joining the series to play Kratos, replacing original actor Ryan Hurst after he was unfortunately injured while filming a stunt for the show. Considering that the show’s first season will presumably be adapting the first Norse-era game, it was uncertain how big of a role Faye would play in the series’ beginning (in GoW 2018, Faye is already deceased and doesn’t appear in flashbacks until God of War: Ragnarok ), but it seems as if the show is directly establishing the importance of her character earlier than expected.

Deborah Ann Woll’s casting comes after a flurry of backlash from select parts of the God of War community earlier this year: the announcement of God of War: Laufey at Sony’s 2026 State of Play , a spinoff game focused exclusively on Faye’s character, was met with some vitriol by fans who were upset at the perceived sidelining of Kratos, a move that some people accused of being motivated by political correctness. Woll, conversely, has been extremely enthused about her role in the games and the opportunity to lead one of her own.

After two games of teasing just how powerful Faye really is, players will finally get to experience it firsthand when Laufey releases next year.

Faye is one of the most consequential characters in the new God of War continuity, setting the events of both games in motion years before they actually happened. She’s powerful enough to go toe-to-toe with Thor himself and end it in a stalemate, and her virtue is displayed in the reverence that the Frost Giants have for the woman who saved them — she’s perhaps one of the most fascinating and well-conceived characters introduced in the two most recent games, and part of that has been Deborah Ann Woll’s dedication to the character. It’s an immense stroke of luck that she decided to return for the Amazon Studios adaptation, both because it’s an affirmation to the fans of how important the source material is, but also because it provides an opportunity for fans to see firsthand just what a fantastic character she really is.

items.title: Prime Video's God of War Live-Action Confirms Major Game Actor
items.summary: A bombshell addition was just made to the live-action God of War series for Prime Video.
items.content:
Image via Sony Santa Monica Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Patrik Walker Published Nov 23, 2026, 12:36 PM EST Patrik Walker is an Emmy Award–winning writer who covers all things Comics & Superheroes. His work can also be found at the Dallas Cowboys, The Sporting News, and CBS Sports, among other outlets. One of the most respected names in his field, he is also a diehard enthusiast of all things comics, anime, gaming and movies — thriving in spaces where discussions involving those or similar topics reign supreme.

Thread 1 Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Wow — the God of War franchise just absolutely did a thing. T he franchise was forced to pivot in a major way with its lead actor following the injury to Ryan Hurst ( Sons of Anarchy ).

Hurst suffered a torn bicep that led to Kratos being recast with Dave Bautista ( Guardians of the Galaxy ), and another major talent has just landed. Better still is it’s not just anyone. It’s someone diehard fans of the God of War video game IP know exceptionally well from her time co-starring in 2018’s God of War game on PS5, and more so in 2022’s God of War: Ragnarok on PS5.

Hurst was transitioning from his voiceover role as Thor in the video game franchise, but Amazon MGM Studios has now added Deborah Ann Woll to reprise her role as Faye (Laufey) in the live-action streaming series for Prime Video.

Faye, the Frost Giant from Jötunheim, second wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus a.k.a. Loki, plays a massive role in the Ragnarok storyline. Securing Deborah Ann Woll guarantees continuity between the IP and live-action adaptation, and also sets the stage for what’s already become a controversial upcoming standalone game, God of War Laufey .

The viral conversation regarding the upcoming God of War Laufey — for whatever reason the aforementioend controversy existed in the first place — failed to acknowledge the fact another Kratos' led adventure is in the pipeline but, before that arrives, Santa Monica Studios gave an update on Faye's headliner.

Laufey, a woman with blonde hair, holding a sword in one hand while the other is surrounded by magic particles. Unfortunately, it's been delayed but, fortunately, the delay isn't an unforgivable one. It's moving from the original release date of February 2027 to May 20, 2027; and Santa Monica Studios made it clear the sole reason is to make the game as flawless as its predecessors.

"Since the reveal of God of War Laufey in June, we’ve been deeply grateful to see so much excitement for Faye’s Journey the Everywhen," they wrote in a press release . "We don’t take for granted the trust placed in the studio to make an extraordinary experience worthy of the passion and dedication to our fans."

They continued: "With this in mind, we’ve made the decision to delay God of War Laufey ’s release to May 20th, 2027. We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential."

A small delay for what should be another epic GOW game, and as Deborah Ann Woll gets ready to bring Faye to the live-action world.

items.title: Deborah Ann Woll Will Play Faye in GOD OF WAR TV Series
items.summary: Deborah Ann Woll will reprise her role of Faye from the games God of War Ragnarok and God of War Laufey in the upcoming live-action show. The post Deborah Ann Woll Will Play Faye in GOD OF WAR TV Seri...
items.content:
Quick Take Deborah Ann Woll has joined the cast of Prime Video's upcoming God of War live-action series.

She'll play the role of Faye, aka Laufey, Kratos' late wife and mother of Atreus.

Woll has played the role in God of War Ragnarok and the upcoming God of War Laufey games.

The game in which she's the main character— God of War Laufey —is still half a year from release. But, Faye as played by Deborah Ann Woll is making her way to live action. Makes sense, really. You have a DAW in the game; why not have her join the TV series? As Deadline reports , the actress we know from Daredevil and True Blood will reprise her roll as Faye, aka Laufey, a powerful Jotunn warrior and wife of Kratos in the God of War Prime Video series .

Woll originally played Faye in 2022's God of War Ragnarok . Laufey will take place concurrently with the story of Ragnarok and the previous 2018 game. It will see "Faye battling through Everywhen as her plans to protect Kratos and their son Atreus are at risk, with her coming into conflict with both Sekhmet and Begtse, the respective gods of war of Egyptian and Mongolian mythologies." Fun!

She joins a very stacked cast for the highly anticipated God of War series. Dave Bautista replaced Ryan Hurst in the role of Kratos following an injury. Other cast members include Mandy Patinkin as Odin, Callum Vinson as Atreus, Ed Skrein as Baldur (of gate fame, I guess), Max Parker as Heimdall, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor, and Teresa Palmer as Sif.

Woll is the second actor from the video games who'll reprise the role in the show. Alastair Duncan plays Mimir in both game and show. In addition to her many roles on TV, Woll recently starred in The Cycle . One of the best horror movies of 2026 if you ask a certain me. No word on whether she'll have much of a place in the MCU following the third and final season of Daredevil: Born Again . But between that and God of War , she's a franchise fave and we'll be watching.

Kyle Anderson is the Senior Editor for Nerdist. You can find his film and TV reviews here . Follow him on Letterboxd .

items.title: God of War Laufey's Faye actor jumps from games to live-action, as Amazon casts Deborah Ann Woll in upcoming series
items.summary: Amazon has cast a second actor from the God of War games for its upcoming live-action series, this time with Deborah Ann Woll reprising her role as Faye.
items.content:
Image credit: Sony News by Kaan Serin Contributor Published on Nov. 23, 2026, 6:09 p.m. 18 comments Follow God of War Laufey Prioritise us on Google After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series.

Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first showed up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey.

Amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir.

Earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course.

There's no release date yet for the show, but it's said to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back.

Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

"We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica said at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon."

While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back , too.

"Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad."

Image: Sony Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 3 Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Production of Prime Video's God of War series is well underway as filming has resumed with Dave Bautista in the role of Kratos . On Monday, Amazon announced another key role has been cast: Deborah Ann Woll will play Faye, a powerful giant warrior and Kratos' wife. Her death kicks off the Norse Saga games.

Woll's name will certainly sound familiar to players of God of War Ragnarök as she's reprising her role from the game. Faye appeared in flashbacks during Ragnarök , which allowed for Kratos to show off a more tender side of himself. She also had a guiding hand in the first game. (She left behind all that yellow paint.)

"Along their journey, Kratos and Atreus discover secrets about Faye that make them wonder how well they truly knew her at all," reads a news release for the Amazon show.

Woll will also star in next year's God of War Laufey , which is due out in May . It will find Faye in the afterlife for gods across various pantheons. When Faye realizes that the plans she laid forth for Kratos and Atreus are in jeopardy, she works to ensure they come to fruition. Fans already have plenty of theories about what events Laufey might cover from Faye's point-of-view.

Image: Sony It's not known yet if the Prime Video TV series will adapt any material from Laufey or if Woll will only appear as Faye in flashback scenes. It's also possible all-new scenes will be written for the show that feature Faye.

Woll is best known for her work in True Blood , Daredevil , and Daredevil: Born Again . She's also guest starred on the actual play series Critical Role and recently appeared in an episode of Polygon's Shelf Quest series.

Prime Video's God of War series does not have a release date at this time.

God of War Laufey is led by one of the most powerful characters in the reboot

items.title: Prime Video’s God Of War Officially Confirms Major Game Actor’s Return
items.summary: It's another hint toward the show's story.
items.content:
Kratos Connecting Emotionally with Atreus in God of War: Ragnarök Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Grant Hermanns Published Nov 23, 2026, 12:07 PM EST Grant Hermanns is a TV News Editor, Interview Host and Reviewer for ScreenRant, having joined the team in early 2021. He got his start in the industry with Moviepilot, followed by working at ComingSoon.net. When not indulging in his love of film/TV, Grant is making his way through his gaming backlog and exploring the world of Dungeons & Dragons with friends. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Dave Bautista will go face-to-face with an iconic game actor for God of War .

Marking the first-ever live-action adaptation of the hit action game franchise, the Prime Video series is specifically adapting the 2018 game in which Kratos and his son Atreus venture through Midgard and ancient Scandinavia to spread the ashes of their wife and mother, Faye, all while Kratos struggles to keep his son's demigod nature a secret. Headed by For All Mankind 's Ronald D. Moore, the God of War series infamously hit a snag when original Kratos actor Ryan Hurst was injured, leading to Dave Bautista taking over the part.

As filming gears up to resume in the near future, Prime Video has announced that the God of War series has officially added Deborah Ann Woll to its cast. The star will be reprising her role of Faye from the recent games, making her the latest major game actor to take part in the series after Ryan Hurst was injured and had to depart his role of Kratos.

Interestingly, while Hurst, who played Thor in 2022's God of War: Ragnarök , was the biggest game actor returning for the series, neither he nor Woll are the only ones coming back. Alastair Duncan is also returning in a recurring fashion as Mímir, the highly-intelligent Norse mythological figure who Kratos and Atreus bring with them on their journey.

Faye sleeps in God of War Laufey. Woll was first introduced in 2018's God of War as Faye , shown in a handful of scenes exploring her and Kratos' relationship prior to her death. As he and Atreus went on their journey to spread her ashes at the highest peak of the nine realms, the pair came to learn that she had a variety of secrets of her own, which further impact Atreus' future as a demigod and the lessons taught by his father.

After returning for more flashbacks in 2022's Ragnarök , Santa Monica Studio took players by surprise when they announced that Woll would be leading her own solo title in God of War: Laufey , slated for a May 20, 2027 release date. The game is set to take part alongside the events of both the 2018 and 2022 games, in which the eponymous character wakes up in the mysterious afterlife-like realm of Everywhen following her funeral and cremation, where she searches for a way to return home to protect Kratos and Atreus.

God of War Ragnarok's story leaves a lot for the player to unpack. Its ending has complex emotions and an unexpected first for the God of War series.

With the confirmation of her casting in the series, it further cements God of War 's plans to stick with adapting the Norse era of the games instead of the Greek era it began with. Given the show comes with a two-season order, it will be interesting to see if, much like HBO's The Last of Us , the Prime Video series elects to expand on Faye's character and backstory with Kratos through flashbacks.

The series will center on series protagonist Kratos, but no other information on the series has been divulged.

items.title: God Of War Ragnarok Is Finally Cheap Enough To Make Me Say “Boy, Buy It”
How to Play the God of War Games in Order
items.summary: Wondering how to play the God of War games in order? We're here to help with a breakdown of the God of War chronology.
items.content:
God of War’s Norse-set masterpieces has cemented it as one of PlayStation’s most iconic franchises . Born during the PS2 era, the God of War franchise made a name for itself with excellent action gameplay, an intriguing tale of divine revenge, and a memorable lead in the Spartan demigod Kratos. 20 years later, God of War has grown into gaming’s seminal action-adventure series, blending that increasingly fine-tuned action with deeper lore and a stronger narrative hook, anchored by an older, more empathic Kratos.

Now that we know the next God of War game will follow Faye in some overlapping timelines, we’ve created this chronology of the series for those interested in playing (or replaying) it from the start.

Sony has released 11 God of War games in the series — seven on home consoles, two on portable consoles, one on mobile, and one text-adventure on Facebook Messenger. A twelfth game, God of War Laufey, was recently announced during a State of Play but does not yet have a release date.

We’re excluding its second mobile release, God of War: Mimir’s Vision, as this AR game doesn’t add to the ongoing narrative but instead provides players with background lore from the world of God of War. We’re also excluding PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale in this chronology, despite its comical inclusion in the God of War canon .

There are several God of War stories told through novels and comics as well, though this list only includes games.

Although technically the first game in the series chronologically was God of War: Ascension, realistically you'll probably want to start with God of War (2018). Not only is it available on both PS4 and PS5, you can also play it on PC. It's a great starting point for anyone just getting into the series.

These blurbs contain mild spoilers for each game, including characters, settings, and story beats.

God of War Sons of Sparta is the latest game in the series, but chronologically it takes place before any of the others. Sons of Sparta acts as a prequel, following the story of Kratos and his brother Deimos as they undertake their brutal training as Spartans. The gameplay breaks fro mthe usual God of War formula in favor of a retro-inspired Metroidvania style.

Available on : PS5 | IGN's God of War Sons of Sparta Review

Ascension , the seventh God of War game by release date but the first chronologically, is a revenge tale that explores the early days of Kratos’s transformation from a Spartan demigod into the God of War.

Ascension takes place months after Kratos was manipulated into killing his wife and daughter by the Greek God of War Ares (more on this under the original God of War section below). Kratos, traumatized by the killings, refuses to honor the oath he swore to Ares, setting into motion the story of Ascension. Ares seeks revenge through the game’s antagonistic Furies, three beings tasked with punishing betrayal, whom Kratos must kill in order to free himself from his oath. The story ends with Kratos leaving his Spartan home behind, still tormented by his grief.

Available on : PS3 | IGN’s God of War: Ascension Review

Kratos’s next adventure is told in the PSP game aptly named God of War: Chains of Olympus . Olympus takes place halfway through Kratos’s ten-year servitude to the gods (five years before God of War) — a servitude that, once completed, will free him from the torturous visions of his past.

The main plot tasks Kratos with rescuing Helios, the Titan God of the Sun, from the underworld at the behest of Athena. There, he encounters the game’s primary antagonist Persephone, Queen of the Underworld. Persephone presents Kratos with an opportunity to reunite with his daughter, and Kratos wrestles with the apocalyptic repercussions of that reunion and his promise to return Helios to the gods.

items.title: God of War Laufey Releases Feb. 16, 2027; Next Kratos-Led Game Coming After It
items.summary: God of War Laufey releases February 16, 2027, as a new Kratos-led game is coming after it and ties to its story.
items.content:
Add as preferred source Revealed two months ago , God of War Laufey is the latest game in the franchise, though one with a new protagonist. If you’re excited to play another entry in the series, you’ll be glad to know we don’t have to wait long to experience it.

Sony has announced that God of War Laufey will be released on PS5 on February 16, 2027!

Not only did we get that info today, but confirmation of the next game after it too.

At San Diego Comic Con (via IGN ), Cory Barlog, studio head of creative at Santa Monica Studio, announced that the next Kratos-led God of War game is coming after Laufey, and connects directly to her story.

No further details were shared, so we don’t know the release date/window, which pantheon the game will be set at, etc. That said, given we saw Kratos make an appearance in God of War Laufey’s reveal gameplay trailer, this is hardly surprising.

For those not caught up to the latest God of War game on the way, Sony explains Laufey’s storyline as:

“Death was supposed to be the end, but for Laufey (Faye), warrior and wife to Kratos, a new adventure is just beginning. Awakening unexpectedly in a strange land after her death, Faye discovers the plans she put in place to protect Kratos and Atreus in her absence are now at risk.

To save the ones she loves, Faye must fight through the afterlife of the gods – the Everywhen – where ruthless gods from across mythology vie for power in a land overflowing with dangerous magic.

Harness Faye’s speed, control and relentlessness to overwhelm even the fiercest of foes with decisive, deadly precision.”

Laufey isn’t really shown in God of War (2018), but she is a “Guardian of the Jötnar, rebel leader against the oppressive Aesir gods, and lone protector of the Wildwoods – Laufey is a warrior whose battle prowess was legendary even among the Giants.”

Expect Laufey to expand the God of War universe, and give the character a proper story since all we saw was her dead at the start of Kratos’ Norse journey.

With God of War Laufey releasing early next year, a God of War Greek mythology remake , and confirmation of a new Kratos-led God of War title coming after Laufey, franchise fans be eating good!

That said, given Laufey is releasing next year, don’t expect a disc-based version of Kratos’ upcoming adventure, since Sony is ceasing physical disc versions of new games at the start of January 2028 . Unless Santa Monica Studio releases two God of War games in a year, which we’re willing to bet money on that it won’t happen.

items.title: All Of The God Of War Games, Ranked From Worst To Best
items.summary: Before God of War Laufey takes us on Faye’s journey, let’s look back at the ups and downs of Kratos’
items.content:
God of War is about to do something it hasn’t done before: center someone other than Kratos. Before we head into the Everywhen as Faye with God of War Laufey , we thought we’d take a look back at over 20 years of god-slaying and navigating Kratos’ dysfunctional family tree by ranking all the previous games from worst to best. Don’t yell at us if your fave is low on the list. Simply swear vengeance upon us and take out a pantheon of gods on the way.

Mechanically, the 2D, sidescrolling Sons of Sparta maybe wasn’t the kind of treatment I want God of War to get but narratively, yes, please, may I have another. I thought turning GOW into a metroidvania was cute, but the gameplay got tedious after a while. However, I adored that the narrative conceit of the game is Kratos telling his daughter Calliope a story about his life as a child. I have so much grief for Kratos’ first family because they wield so much narrative power over this entire franchise but we know so little about them. Regardless of the gameplay, I’m glad Sons of Sparta exists so I can get my “Kratos being a good dad to his FIRST child for a change” fix. — Ash Parrish

The last PS3 God of War is absolutely a relic of a pre-live-service era when companies were bolting multiplayer modes onto the sides of their most lucrative ships, so it’s not super surprising that the bulk of Ascension feels a little underbaked. The prequel is still full of the kinds of incredible, cinematic set pieces and twitchy action that make each God of War at least memorable, but its hack-and-slash combat feels narrowly focused on Kratos’ iconic Blades of Chaos, with you shifting between different elemental affinities instead of different weapons that would have more tangibly changed up your playstyle and the flow of combat. That final boss fight against the Kraken and the Furies still whips pretty hard, though. — Kenneth Shepard

God of War Ragnarok would have been incredible as two games instead of one. Yeah, the frustratingly bloated and overly long sequel is still rock solid, with fantastic action and some incredible moments, especially for Kratos and Atreus, who remain the heart and soul of the series’ Norse mythology games despite the ever-expanding cast. Still, it’s hard to not get wistful thinking of what this story might’ve looked like if it’d had a bit of breathing room. Ragnarok ’s Valhalla DLC, meanwhile, shows exactly what a hypothetical scaled-back sequel could have looked like by giving Kratos a roguelike therapy session that’s laser-focused on one character instead of a dozen, which helps the core action mechanics shine through in a way that base Ragnarok didn’t, having a bit too much noise going on to let that action sing sometimes. It’s a shame because so many of Ragnarok ’s narrative threads, such as Angrboda seeking out the remnants of the frost giants and the inner machinations of Thor’s family drama, are genuinely compelling, but it’s all fighting for attention in a game that’s trying to wrap up a trilogy’s-worth of stories in a second game. — Kenneth Shepard

The PlayStation Portable was one of the earlier attempts at a handheld offering console-level experiences, and God of War: Chains of Olympus was certainly one of the best examples of a studio making it happen. Ready at Dawn pulled off a handheld God of War remarkably well, creating a Kratos experience that was pretty comparable to its console brethren and that you could take on the go. Though it isn’t quite as narratively illuminating as its sequel, it’s still a truly impressive feat for 2008. — Kenneth Shepard

Ghost of Sparta , Ready at Dawn’s second Chaos Blade swing at a handheld God of War game, is just as solid a game as its predecessor. What gives it a bit of an edge over Chains of Olympus is how much we learn about Kratos in the prequel, including the introduction of his brother Deimos, who adds a whole new wrinkle to Kratos’ dysfunctional family tree. That guy is an onion of layers to peel back, and Ready at Dawn was cooking every time it got the keys to the kitchen. — Kenneth Shepard

Remembering the original God of War 21 years after its 2005 launch feels quaint in a way that makes me uncomfortable with my advancing age. I remember when this game came out; I played it then. But viewing this game now, in the context of what the series has grown into, is bewildering. Voiced by T.C. Carson and equipped with a double jump, this Kratos is a completely different person in a completely different type of game. OG God of War bleeds mid-aughts edginess. The game’s opening shot features a morose Kratos yeeting himself off a cliff, and every female character has her breasts out, just because. That said, the original God of War was a great action platformer with the kind of bloody, violent combat we craved in the mid-aughts. — Ash Parrish

God of War III felt big enough to shoulder the weight of being the “last” major game in the franchise at the time. It contained a “resolution” to Kratos’ story that featured some pretty interesting commentary on the nature and purpose of hope, even if it wasn’t executed that well. God of War III is the franchise’s first flirtation with the “Give Kratos a lil guy to look after” mechanic as Pandora, she of the famous box, tags along for part of your adventure. Chatty sidekicks who help you open doors were already a thing by the time this game came out in 2010, but I wasn’t sure how well the famously dour Kratos would work with the bright and chipper Pandora. And y’know what, he did pretty good. There’s a moment when Zeus hurts Pandora and the camera cuts to Kratos who’s wearing the biggest, ugliest frown, as though all the sliders on his face model were cranked all the way down, and I believed it. I was on his side. — Ash Parrish

God of War II improves on the original in every way with a bigger story and bloodier combat. I really enjoyed the smart, narrative way the game depowers Kratos to set him up to receive new weapons and abilities. Fighting the Colossus of Rhodes, the opening battle in God of War II , is one of the greater gameplay sequences of the PS2 era. Incredibly cinematic and bombastic— you’re fighting the Greek mythological equivalent of a Gundam after all— the fight really conveys what a godly struggle should be, a neat escalation of the mortal battles of the first game. — Ash Parrish

God of War ’s Norse-themed reboot was risky. It changed everything we knew about what it meant to embody Kratos, primarily by acting as a metatextual critique of what the series had once been. A somber, shame-ridden Kratos has retreated to the Nine Realms after slaughtering the Greek pantheon, and rather than flaunting those acts, he attempts to hide them away from his son Atreus before confronting his past and choosing to believe that how things have been is not how they must be. The original God of War games were very much of a different era, one in which edgy, violent excess sold copies. As tastes have changed, God of War had to as well if it was going to thrive, and the 2018 reboot does so not by pretending what came before didn’t happen, but instead by using Kratos’ decade of rage as a springboard to become something greater.

And boy, did it become something greater on the mechanical front, too. Kratos trades his Blades of Chaos (initially) for an icy Leviathan Axe that makes the game feel heavier and more challenging, and the series adopts RPG-lite elements to offer more chances for player expression than the original games were ever capable of. With this reboot, Santa Monica Studio sought to reinvent everything God of War ever was, from its ethos to its best-in-class combat, and it succeeded. — Kenneth Shepard

items.content:
• Add more error checking and logging for NVIDIA Streamline
  • Add entries in settings.ini for controlling for NVIDIAStreamlineLog, NVIDIAStreamlineOTAUpdates NVIDIAStreamlineLog=Off ; Values: Off, Default, Verbose NVIDIAStreamlineOTAUpdates=On ; Values: Off, On
  • When NVIDIAStreamlineLog enabled, a log file in the Save Game directory will be generated and overwritten every launch. If encountering errors, please submit a support ticket including this log. C:\Users\\Saved Games\God of War Ragnarök\sl.log

items.title: Black Screen Launch Issue Hotfix
items.summary: An NVIDIA Driver Crash/Soft Lock that prevents the game from loading is under investigation. In the meantime, we've implemented a work around for the cause of the crash to change how shader compilation works. This change may cause some micr
items.content:
An NVIDIA Driver Crash/Soft Lock that prevents the game from loading is under investigation. In the meantime, we've implemented a work around for the cause of the crash to change how shader compilation works. This change may cause some micro-stuttering during initial load, but will hopefully avoid the driver crash that prevents game from starting.

Please verify files after patching.

items.title: Patch 9 - 20th Anniversary Update
items.summary: As a gift to everyone who owns God of War Ragnarök, the Dark Odyssey collection is now available in-game at no additional cost! Inspired by the working name of God of War (2005) and the skin that originally appeared in God of War II as a re
items.content:
As a gift to everyone who owns God of War Ragnarök, the Dark Odyssey collection is now available in-game at no additional cost! Inspired by the working name of God of War (2005) and the skin that originally appeared in God of War II as a reward for beating the game on God Mode difficulty, we have brought back the black and gold theme for the anniversary.

Dark Odyssey Collection

Dark Odyssey Armor & Appearance for Kratos
  • Dark Odyssey Kratos Appearance
  • Dark Odyssey Armor Set for Kratos (Dark Odyssey Breastplate, Dark Odyssey Bracers, Dark Odyssey Belt)
Dark Odyssey Companion Armor
  • Dark Odyssey Vestment for Atreus
  • Dark Odyssey Witch Frock for Freya
Dark Odyssey Weapon Appearances & Attachments*
  • Dark Odyssey Leviathan Axe & Dark Odyssey Knob
  • Dark Odyssey Blades of Chaos & Dark Odyssey Handles
  • Dark Odyssey Draupnir Spear & Dark Odyssey Hind
Dark Odyssey Shield Appearances & Rönd
  • Dark Odyssey Guardian Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Dauntless Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Stone Wall Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Shatter Start Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Onslaught Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Spartan Aspis Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Rönd
*Please note, the weapon appearances are made for the fully upgraded version of each weapon and will only be available for use upon reaching that upgrade.

Edit Appearance for Weapon & Shield Attachments

With the addition of the new Dark Odyssey weapon attachments and shield rönd in the patch, we have added the ability to use the ‘Edit Appearance’ feature on those components of Kratos’ arsenal. You’ll be able to pick whatever visual suits your look with the functionality you want for your build!
